answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grade trust like a garden, not a gate: every identity starts fallow and must earn standing through verified, useful work over many epochs, with its record weighted by recency so old deeds fade. Creating a thousand fake identities gains nothing, because each starts at zero and must pay the same slow cost in real work before it can vote or claim rewards. An attacker who floods the garden finds each fable of a trusted agent collapses under the same proof burden, while a shale layer of slashed stake beneath offenders makes mass fabrication costly.
